title: Enterprise variant intake routing and gated onboarding policy
text:
Enterprise variant intake routing and gated onboarding policy

description:
Create a repeatable intake and routing rubric for customer-submitted model variants (new models, quantized variants, and version pin requests) that balances enterprise stability requirements with speed-to-onboard. This ticket defines: 1) intake signals + auto-routing rules, 2) a gated evaluation pipeline (smoke tests, regression evals, privacy/compliance checklist), 3) pin/deprecation policy templates, and 4) clear handoffs to Eng/Research/Trust for canary and rollout. Goal: reduce ad-hoc triage meetings, provide predictable SLAs for enterprise customers, and enforce safety/compliance gates before variants are allowed in Dedicated/Private lanes.

acceptance_criteria:
Intake form fields standardized and implemented in intake UI (request metadata, customer use-case, sensitivity level, SLA requirements, attestation links).
Routing rules documented and tested (auto-route to Fast-Shadow, Enterprise Review, or Low-Risk Catalog lanes based on signals).
Eval gate checklist created with pass/fail criteria and automated smoke tests wired into pipeline.
Pin/deprecation templates approved by Legal and Security and integrated into catalog metadata.
Handoff runbook that lists responsibilities for Eng, Research, Trust, and Solutions is published and linked from ticket.

steps:
Draft intake signal taxonomy and scoring (sensitivity, traffic footprint, model provenance, quantization level).
Prototype routing rules in intake service (rules defined as prioritized list + thresholds).
Define eval gate suite: functional regressions, latency/cost profile, OOD safety tests, privacy checklist, third-party attestations.
Design pin semantics (soft-pin vs hard-pin), deprecation windows, and backward-compatibility contract.
Run 2 pilot onboardings from customer requests (one quantized variant, one major version pin) and iterate on checklist.

comments:
2026-03-02 | Maya Chen: Initial draft of taxonomy posted to Confluence. Highlights: sensitivity, customer SLA, model provenance. Asked Eng for feasibility check on routing thresholds.
2026-03-05 | Arjun Patel: Met with Eng infra — continuous intake routing is feasible but we need a feature flag for staged rollout. Action: ENG to provide estimate for flag and routing UI changes. Assigned ENG-18544.
2026-03-08 | Sofia Martinez (Trust): Reviewed eval checklist. Request to add data retention attestation and E2E audit log requirement for Private deployments. Marked security_review_required = true.
2026-03-10 | Arjun Patel: Pilot customers identified (AcmePayments, HealthStack). Created pilot timeline and test matrices. Added cost/latency SLO checks to acceptance criteria.
2026-03-12 | Research (Liam O'Connor): Proposed compatibility signature idea — deterministic fingerprint of tokenizer/config to detect silent incompatibilities. Will prototype smoke-check in pipeline.
2026-03-14 | Maya Chen: Draft pin semantics circulated. Key decision: soft-pin allowed for 30 days with automatic telemetry-based extension; hard-pin requires Contract & Legal sign-off. Next: legal review on deprecation notices.

next_steps:
ENG: Implement feature flag + routing rule prototype (ENG-18544) — due 2026-03-21.
Research: Prototype compatibility signature smoke-test and submit PR to evals pipeline by 2026-03-22.
Trust/Security: Finalize privacy attestation template and sign-off on pin/deprecation language by 2026-03-25.
PM: Run two pilot onboards and collect telemetry and feedback; iterate on checklist by 2026-03-31.

notes_and_tradeoffs:
Tradeoff: stricter eval gates reduce risk but increase time-to-onboard. We default to an adaptive lane: 'Fast-Shadow' for non-sensitive workloads with automated rollback tokens; 'Enterprise Review' for high-sensitivity or SLAs.
Decision: implement soft-pin default (30d) to reduce friction; provide an upgrade path to hard-pin for customers with contractual needs.
Open question: how to correlate downstream application regression signal with model variants in-hosted vs dedicated lanes. Proposed: unique rollout token in request headers for traceability.
